overall_assessment.realism: The samples are highly realistic and detailed, reflecting plausible attack scenarios in adversarial machine learning. The technical data includes credible commit logs with appropriate timestamps, author formats, and commit messages that align with the described poisoning activities. The example poisoned sample metadata contains believable file names, checksums, and modification descriptions consistent with the attack vectors. Training and inference log excerpts show logical progression and effects of poisoning, such as label distribution shifts and increased error rates. The included Python code snippets are syntactically correct and demonstrate practical poisoning implementations. Indicators and detection methods are well-aligned with current research and operational practices. The use of MITRE ATT&CK technique identifiers further grounds the scenarios in recognized threat frameworks.
overall_assessment.consistency: The entries maintain uniform structure and adhere strictly to the provided schema. Each sample includes the required keys: scenario, technical_data (with nested commit logs, sample metadata, pipeline and inference logs, and code), indicators, detection_method, and relevant_mitre_techniques. Data types are consistent (strings, arrays, nested objects), and timestamps follow ISO 8601 format. The example poisoned sample metadata fields correspond appropriately to the domain (audio or email). The log excerpts and code snippets are coherent and contextually relevant. The embedding and MFCC vector snippets use plausible placeholder formats. Overall, the samples are internally consistent and schema-compliant.
